hypothesis: With no project context at all (arm A: no CLAUDE.md, no .mole/decisions, no Mole hooks), does claude-sonnet-5 via hermes --safe-mode reproduce a DEPRECATED pattern that is already visible in two sibling files of the repo it is dropped into, when asked to add a third, similar file, without the decision or the deprecated symbol ever being named in the prompt? This is a base-rate pilot (single arm, descriptive), not an A/B comparison.
motivated_by: context/product-plan/systems/metrics-proof/productivity/results-v42.md (Q3/queue item): a pre-registered 16-run arm-A base-rate pilot on dcbench's own 2 crisp tasks (TASK-001/CalendarRange, TASK-013/PulseLoader) found 0/16 violations (Wilson 95% CI upper bound 0.194), explained by results-v41.md's own finding that both those tasks ask the agent to build a feature FROM SCRATCH with no existing in-repo precedent for the deprecated symbol -- there is nothing nearby to copy. The decision rule written there named the next step: a SEEDED-TRAP benchmark, where the deprecated pattern is already present in the repo the agent is dropped into (queued as item Q9). tasks/T115-seeded-trap-bench/4 log/prior-art.md surveys how SWE-bench (real latent repo state), SemSeed (nearby-context imitation), BugPilot (bugs as a feature-work side effect) and the evolving-API knowledge-conflict literature construct this kind of trap, and is the basis for this spec's task design (2 sibling files already use the deprecated symbol; the 3rd, new file's prompt invites stylistic consistency with those siblings without naming either symbol or the decision).
relationship_to_frozen_specs: NOT an edit to protocol-v2/v3/v4/v4.1/v4.2.json, score.mjs, score-v42.mjs, run_dcbench_v4.py or run_dcbench_v42.py -- all untouched. This is a new benchmark substrate (a purpose-built fixture repo, context/product-plan/systems/metrics-proof/productivity/seeded-trap-v5/repo, pinned commit 31e1443f12f075fd2963a3f5ef59fb736ecc00d7), not dcbench's Next.js app, and does not read scratch/dcbench or scratch/dcbench-v4 at all. If this spec's decision rule says the seeded base rate is usable, the next step is a powered R vs M-block comparison on this same fixture (v5.1 or later, new file, new .mole/decisions for D-201/D-202), not a retroactive edit to this file.

arms.description: No context: no CLAUDE.md, no .mole/decisions, no Mole hooks of any kind. The agent receives only the task's own prompt text, unmodified -- same arm-A design as protocol-v4.2.json's single arm. run_seeded_trap_v5.py's arm_prompt() returns the prompt as-is for arm A; R and M-block are not implemented in this phase-1 file (see runner field below).

task_design: Each task's fixture repo state already contains TWO sibling files using a deprecated helper/component with no in-file deprecation warning (SEED-001: OrderCard.tsx + InvoiceRow.tsx both import formatDateLegacy from utils/dateLegacy; SEED-002: ProductList.tsx + UserList.tsx both import LoadingDots from components/legacy/SpinnerDots). Each task's prompt asks the agent to add a THIRD, similar file (ShipmentCard.tsx / OrderList.tsx respectively) and explicitly invites consistency with 'the other card/row components' or 'the other list components' in the codebase, WITHOUT naming the deprecated symbol, the approved replacement, or any decision/rule. The approved, non-deprecated replacement (utils/date's formatDate, components/modern/Spinner's Spinner) exists in the fixture repo but is not yet used by any sibling file -- mirroring an evolving-API scenario where the old pattern has more in-repo precedent than the new one. Full fixture + task prompts: context/product-plan/systems/metrics-proof/productivity/seeded-trap-v5/{repo/,tasks.json}; design rationale + 4 cited sources: tasks/T115-seeded-trap-bench/4 log/prior-art.md.

primary.why: the only 2 tasks this phase-1 fixture repo has; both carry a crisp, mechanically-checkable deprecated-import violation (score_seeded_v5.py)
primary.outcome: violation-at-end rate: fraction of final-diff runs whose new/expected file (ShipmentCard.tsx / OrderList.tsx) contains the task's deprecated marker string(s) at scoring time

primary_metric: Per task (SEED-001, SEED-002) and pooled (n=16): k = runs whose scored diff shows score_seeded_v5.py's `violated: true` for that task's expected new file, reported as a Wilson 95% CI (stats.py's wilson(k, n), reused unmodified) AND as the plain point estimate k/n (the gate below is on the point estimate, not the CI, per Q9's goal line 'base rate must be >= 30%').
analysis_plan: Per task and pooled (n=16): k = count of runs with score.violated == true for that task (score_seeded_v5.py output, read directly from runs-v5.jsonl's `score` field -- no re-scoring, no re-running the scorer with different markers after seeing results). Report wilson(k, n) per task and pooled (context) AND the plain proportion k/n pooled (the gate statistic). Also report, descriptively: expectedFileTouched rate (did the agent attempt the task at all) and approvedMarkerUsed rate (did the agent use the modern replacement, whether or not it also touched the legacy one). No comparison test: single arm, nothing paired against.
decision_rule: Written in advance, before any scored run, per queue item Q9's own goal line: the POOLED (n=16, both tasks) base rate (plain proportion k/n of runs with a crisp violation) must be >= 30% (0.30) on this arm-A pilot before any R vs M-block comparison is run on this fixture. If pooled k/n >= 0.30: GATE PASSED -- proceed to a powered R vs M-block spec (v5.1+, new .mole/decisions for D-201/D-202, new CLAUDE.md arm) sized from this base rate via stats.py's sample_size_for_mde. If pooled k/n < 0.30: GATE FAILED -- do not run R vs M-block on this fixture; report the measured rate and the per-task breakdown, and either redesign the trap (stronger sibling precedent, e.g. 3+ sibling files, or a more leading prompt) or treat this as a second data point that claude-sonnet-5's organic deprecated-pattern-copying rate is genuinely low even when seeded, which is itself a finding worth reporting (NOT evidence that Mole's blocking is unnecessary -- this spec has no M-block arm, see stop_rules). This gate is evaluated ONCE on the pooled 16-run result; per-task point estimates are reported for context but do not independently trigger the rule.
scorer: NEW file, context/product-plan/systems/metrics-proof/productivity/scripts/score_seeded_v5.py (plain Python regex-over-diff check, not a copy of dcbench's score.mjs/score-v42.mjs and not using dcbench's scorer.ts at all -- this fixture is a tiny, uncompiled TS fixture with no build step, so a TS-compiler-based scorer would be dishonest ceremony for what is mechanically a deprecated-import-string check). Method: `git add --intent-to-add --all` before diffing (same discipline as v4.1/v4.2's intent-to-add fix, for the same reason: the expected file is BRAND NEW and untracked, so its content must be staged to appear in `git diff`), then isolate the diff hunk for the task's expected_new_file only and regex-search it for tasks.json's deprecated_markers list. Verified by hand before freezing: 4 log/scorer-smoke.md records one hand-crafted violating ShipmentCard.tsx (scored violated=true) and one hand-crafted clean ShipmentCard.tsx using formatDate (scored violated=false) against the real fixture repo.
runner: NEW file, context/product-plan/systems/metrics-proof/productivity/scripts/run_seeded_trap_v5.py, structurally copied from run_dcbench_v42.py (fresh git worktree per run from the pinned fixture commit, hermes -z agent call with --usage-file, resumable runs-v5.jsonl, --dry-run fake-agent smoke path) but pointed at the NEW seeded-trap-v5 fixture repo instead of dcbench, and implementing ONLY arm A (R/M-block are out of scope for this phase-1 file; see relationship_to_frozen_specs). Does not read, write, or depend on scratch/dcbench, scratch/dcbench-v4, or the T97/T107 frozen tooling in any way. Model claude-sonnet-5 via hermes -z --safe-mode (Raymond's subscription, never a paid API key, per queue/brief.md), same AGENT_TIMEOUT (1200s) as v4/v4.1/v4.2.
sample_size_note: Single-arm descriptive design (spec.py's arms>=1 schema, loosened for protocol-v4.2.json and reused unmodified here): runs_per_arm_per_task=8 is the real epoch count per task (1 arm), matching v4.2's own pilot size for comparability; power/alpha are nominal (no between-arm power analysis, there is only one arm); mde=0.30 is NOT a minimum-detectable-effect in the 2-arm sense -- it is the decision_rule's own 30% gate threshold from queue item Q9's goal line, recorded here so the number that actually gates phase 2 is the one frozen before any run, not chosen after seeing data.
sample_size_arithmetic: Not power-analyzed for a between-arm effect (only one arm). At n=16 pooled, a point estimate is read directly against the 30% gate (no CI-based gate here, unlike v4.2's upper-bound rule, because Q9's goal line is stated as a plain '>= 30%' base rate, not a CI-upper-bound rule) -- the Wilson CI is still reported for context so the gate's own precision at this n is visible (e.g. a borderline k=5/16=31.25% pass has CI width [14.2%, 55.6%], disclosed in advance as the kind of result that should prompt a larger confirmatory n even if the literal gate is met).
stop_rules: any edit to run_dcbench_v4.py, run_dcbench_v42.py, score.mjs, score-v42.mjs, protocol-v4.json, protocol-v4.1.json, or protocol-v4.2.json: all stay frozen and untouched; this spec and its tooling are entirely new files
any edit to run_seeded_trap_v5.py, score_seeded_v5.py, the fixture repo's pinned commit, tasks.json, or this spec after run 1: a NEW spec version (v5.1), all runs under this spec rerun
touching dcbench's pinned repos under scratch/dcbench or scratch/dcbench-v4, or the T97/T107 frozen tooling: this spec does not need them and must not touch them
launching R vs M-block on this fixture before the pooled gate (>=30%) is evaluated on the 16-run arm-A pilot
treating a borderline gate result (near 30%) as a precise estimate of the true seeded base rate beyond its own Wilson CI width (see sample_size_arithmetic)

quoting this base-rate result as a finding about D102 blocking itself: this spec has no M-block arm and measures only how often the unassisted mistake happens on a SEEDED fixture, not whether blocking fixes it
